sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant after referring to deposition of applicant witness Dr. PD Soni and per permanent disability certificate Ex.P/23 submits that appellant suffered 9 % permanent disability but Tribunal has determined only 4 % permanent disability.
Hence, permanent disability be determined as 9%.
Appellant is working as bus operator and no amount has been awarded for loss of future treatment.
Therefore, compensation awarded by the Tribunal be suitably enhanced.
3. Learned counsel for the respondent insurance company submits that in the instant case, appellant is working as bus operator.
Therefore, it cannot be said that he has suffered any functional disability.
Therefore, no amount under the head of loss of future earning capacity can be awarded.
On above grounds, it is urged that appeal filed by the appellants be dismissed.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
5. So far as loss of future earning capacity is concerned, admittedly, Dr. PD Soni has deposed that appellant has suffered 9% permanent disability.
In the instant case, admittedly, appellant is working as bus operator.
Tribunal has determined 4% functional permanent disability and has accordingly awarded loss of future earning capacity.

In this Court's opinion, in view of nature of permanent disability and looking to the nature of job of appellant, no interference is required in the findings recorded by the Tribunal under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
6. So far as expenses for future treatment is concerned, there is nothing on record to show that appellant requires any further future treatment.
Therefore, no amount under the head of future treatment can be awarded.
Perusal of impugned award reveals that Tribunal has not awarded any amount for loss of amenities.
Hence, in view of law laid down in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343, in this Court's opinion, appellant is entitled to receive Rs.50,000/- for loss of amenities.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. Hence, in view of above, appeal filed by the appellant is partly allowed to the extent as indicated herein above and appellant is entitled to receive Rs.50000/- over and above awarded by the Tribunal.
8.
Enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate determined by the Tribunal.
Other findings of the Tribunal shall remain intact.
9. Accordingly, appeal is disposed off.
